scope.flow: UniswapPriceOracle TWAP validation used as pre-swap price check in BuyBackBurner V2 buyback path

statements.text: _validatePrice() must protect the buyback mechanism from price manipulation by comparing the current spot price against a time-weighted average price derived from two snapshots taken at different points in time.
A correct TWAP implementation must store a previous cumulative price reading and compare it against the current cumulative price, not use the same reading as both starting point and reference.
The V2 buyback path must retain an effective pre-swap price validation so that a manipulated spot price is rejected before the swap executes.
buyBack() has no access control and is callable by anyone.
The attacker flash-loans tokens to manipulate the Uniswap V2 pool reserves.
The attacker calls buyBack(), and _validatePrice() passes regardless of the manipulation.
The swap executes at the manipulated price with amountOutMin = 0, accepting any output.

The TWAP computation reduces to (tradePrice × elapsedTime) / elapsedTime = tradePrice because cumulativePriceLast is read from the pool and used as both the starting point and the reference for subtraction in the same calculation, so timeWeightedAverage always equals tradePrice.

Because timeWeightedAverage always equals tradePrice, the derivation calculation always produces zero, and zero is always less than or equal to any slippage parameter, so the validation always returns true.

The post-swap bounds check compares the post-swap price against bounds derived from previousPrice, which was captured after validatePrice passes at the already-manipulated spot price, anchoring the check to the wrong baseline.

ambiguities: Report does not state a concrete numeric slippage parameter or swap amount, so the maxSlippage% bound is qualitative.
Report does not establish a prior stored cumulative price snapshot existing before the checked call; the missing two-snapshot state is described as the required fix, not an existing precondition.
Whether the attacker's profit is realized in the same transaction as the buyBack() call is not explicitly stated beyond the flash-loan/restore sequence.
